summary: Delta re-adjudication of jet EC (59 cases) after the fill cycle (bcab4931a/0d151b0ad/b5e65a454). The predecessor's two blocking findings — cases 1839 and 1840 misbinding capability_id=bundler-production-build for CommonJS/module.exports assertions — are RESOLVED in the current source, verified by reading the files directly (not trusting the fill report): behavior/1839.md line 15 and behavior/1840.md line 15 both now bind capability_id: library-build-publishing, and aw.toml [[aw.ec.generated.cases]] agrees (lines 12 and 26). The rebind is semantically correct: library-build-publishing's Promise explicitly emits CommonJS ('library mode (ESM + optional CJS ...)', README line 362) whereas bundler-production-build is app-mode `jet build` and never emits CJS — so coverage now attaches to the only capability that can produce the artifact under test. The prior non-blocking traceability observation (a) is closed: all three claims now have work-root rows under the library-build-publishing section (README lines 381/382/383 — #1839 planned, #1840 planned, #1784 implemented/verified), with honest maturity columns. Spot-check confirms the fill did not disturb neighboring content: assertions in 1839.md/1840.md/1784.md are preserved verbatim and match aw.toml (lines 21, 34-35, 289-290) exactly; claim_id/contract_id/category/td_ref are consistent across .md and aw.toml; bundler-production-build retains its own five legitimately-bound cases (asset-sourcemap-negative-paths, bundler-production-readiness, production-bundle-output-parity, scss-sass-compilation, transform-resolver-parity), so no dimension regressed. Six-axis verdict at delta depth: (1) capability_claim_coverage TRUE — each of claims 1839/1840/1784 has exactly one covering case now bound to the CJS-emitting capability, with resolving work-root rows; (2) required_dimensions TRUE — all three are category:behavior under DeveloperTool library-build-publishing (Required Verification: smoke/conformance/corpus/negative), no dimension left empty by the move; (3) assertions_specific TRUE — 1839 pins 'every named source export through module.exports while excluding default', 1840 pins 'the const on module.exports under that export name', both concrete and falsifiable; 1784 is a robustness/negative assertion consistent with the accepted negative-case bar (cf. asset-sourcemap-negative-paths); (4) oracle_independent TRUE — the oracles are black-box observations of the emitted CJS artifact's module.exports, external to the bundler internals under test and not `aw ec` itself; (5) loopholes_checked TRUE — 'every ... while excluding default' and the named-collision scenario resist trivial/degenerate satisfaction; (6) false_green_risk_checked TRUE at the contract layer — the assertions require observing real emitted output that a faithful generator cannot satisfy with zero assertions. Non-blocking, carried forward (NOT a blocker, and NOT fixable by `aw ec fill`): the gate commands `cargo test -p jet --test behavior_ec_1839|behavior_ec_1840|behavior_jet_mangle_utf8_safety -- --ignored` target scaffolds `aw ec gen` has not yet produced (apps/jet/tests/behavior_ec_*.rs do not exist), so today the gate fails closed (cargo errors on a missing test target — RED, not false-green). The residual #694-class vacuity risk — that `aw ec gen` could emit an empty `#[ignore]` scaffold whose `-- --ignored` run passes with zero real assertions — is structurally downstream of EC acceptance and is enforced by `aw ec gen --verify` + the health test gate, not by this semantic contract review; it must be checked when gen produces the fixture bodies. This is agent arbitration input recorded truthfully as reviewer_kind: agent (agent-backed submission authorized for this run); it is not human acceptance evidence.
